ph-smmarkets.name: basketwatch-vet-smmarkets
ph-smmarkets.significance: Proves a spa_empty site is fully workable through Studio. The page serves no price in raw HTML even through the Web Unlocker, yet the Studio scraper - which drives a real browser - returned a clean contract-shaped row on the first try, no healing needed.

us-dierbergs.name: basketwatch-vet-dierbergs
us-dierbergs.significance: Authentic US regional grocer, json-ld, real basket staple (bread). Confirms the server_rendered tier of the registry end to end.

ph-shopgaisano.name: basketwatch-vet-shopgaisano
ph-shopgaisano.significance: Top-scoring PH site (100) and the strongest PH grocery target: json-ld, 10/10 basket categories off a 1,406-URL sitemap. The row is rice per 5kg, which is the PH basket anchor item named in docs/prd.md section 5. Also picked up in_stock=false correctly, so stock state is not being faked.

locked_fleet._comment: The LOCKED Basketwatch fleet. This file is the decision, not a suggestion: score.py renders registry.md from it and fails loudly if a locked site is no longer fleet-ready. Change the fleet by editing this file, never by re-running a picker.
locked_fleet.rationale: Eight real stores, four per country, spanning five extraction shapes (json-ld, graphql, bare-html, spa-with-state, spa-opaque) so a breakage in one does not resemble a breakage in another. Weighted toward genuine grocers over online pantries per docs/prd.md section 2.6, and toward sites already proven end to end. Clears the PRD bar of 4+ US scrapers plus the clone store, with PH included. Members split into two roles. Index contributors supply the basket on both sides. The US source is ethnic grocers, which stock generic staples and fresh produce where the supermarket chains publish nothing and the online pantries sell diet goods. Reliability subjects scrape cleanly across different markup shapes and carry the self-healing story without feeding the index.

fleet.name: Shop Gaisano
fleet.why_locked: Top-scoring site in the whole registry. Server-rendered json-ld, 10/10 basket categories off a 1,406-URL sitemap, Visayas/Mindanao regional chain with no prebuilt scraper anywhere. Proven end to end on rice 5kg, the PH basket anchor item.

fleet.name: Ever Supermarket
fleet.why_locked: Best basket coverage of any store in the registry: 10/10 core items, 19/20 tracked, every one with a computed unit price, and genuine staples throughout - Farmboy Pandan Rice 5kg, whole chicken 1kg, a 30-egg tray. Shopify search makes selection reliable.
fleet.caveat: Was scored 85/backup on sitemap-derived basket coverage of 0/10. Its catalogue was only visible through Shopify search - a reminder that sitemap coverage understates any store with a search API.

fleet.name: Shop Suki
fleet.why_locked: 16 of 20 items settled with strong picks - Nestle Fresh Milk 1L, Angelina Super Loaf 640g, Balducci Spaghetti 500g, real white onions sold by weight, Absolute Distilled Water 6L. Server-rendered json-ld and a broad staples catalogue.
fleet.caveat: Its chicken pick is Marca Manok Sinandomeng Rice - 'manok' is the brand, not the contents - and its eggs pick is salted egg. Both need curating in manual-basket.json before use.

fleet.name: SM Markets
fleet.why_locked: Largest PH supermarket network and the broadest PH catalogue. Pages are a client-rendered shell, but the public Magento GraphQL endpoint is a structured fallback no selector change can break. Proven end to end.

fleet.name: MerryMart Wholesale
fleet.why_locked: Fully server-rendered PHP prices with no structured data at all - the bare-HTML shape the fleet otherwise lacks on the PH side, and the one most likely to break on a redesign, which makes it a good heal subject.
fleet.caveat: Wholesale case pricing. Needs per-unit normalisation before its numbers enter the basket index.

fleet.name: Landers Superstore
fleet.why_locked: 10/10 basket categories from a 17,032-URL sitemap - the deepest basket coverage of any PH site - and a well-known consumer name for the demo.
fleet.caveat: Highest-risk member. Prices render client-side and the backing APIs (api.landers.ph, Unbxd search) are private, so there is no non-browser fallback. If its Studio scraper proves flaky, swap in Southstar Drug, which is server-rendered microdata.

fleet.name: Kesar Grocery
fleet.why_locked: The US index source. 13 of 20 items settled, 7/10 core, every one unit-priced, and genuinely generic goods including fresh produce: Basmati 4LB, whole wheat bread 24oz, Great Value elbow pasta 1LB, Amul cheese 1KG, organic bananas 3lb, beefsteak tomatoes, white onions, gala apples, navel oranges. 11,987 products in its sitemap and no structured data at all, which is why it needed bare-HTML extraction to surface.
fleet.caveat: Its cooking-oil pick is almond oil rather than a neutral cooking oil; curate before use. Bare-HTML extraction means no structured data to fall back on, so a redesign hits harder here than on a json-ld site - which also makes it a good heal subject.

fleet.name: MexGrocer
fleet.why_locked: Second US index source and a different cuisine, so the two do not share supply. 9 items settled, 5/10 core, Shopify search for reliable selection. Mahatma Long Grain Rice and Cafe de Olla ground coffee are real staples.
fleet.caveat: Blocked on plain HTTP for page fetches but its Shopify search API answers fine. Chicken resolves to bouillon and bananas to banana leaves; both need curating.

fleet.name: Dierbergs
fleet.why_locked: Authentic St. Louis regional grocer with clean json-ld and real basket staples. Proven end to end on a bread SKU.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

fleet.name: The Fresh Market
fleet.why_locked: Specialty national grocer, 9/10 basket categories, server-rendered json-ld reachable without the Unlocker. Highest-scoring authentic US grocer after Dierbergs.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

fleet.name: Wegmans
fleet.why_locked: Major regional grocer that ships prices inside embedded page state rather than markup - a distinct extraction shape from the json-ld sites, and a realistic breakage mode.
fleet.caveat: Only 4/10 basket categories surfaced from its sitemap; confirm SKU coverage before relying on it for the index.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

fleet.name: Meijer
fleet.why_locked: Midwest supercenter, 8/10 basket categories, plain HTML pricing with no structured data - the bare-HTML shape on the US side. Promoted from the bench after Grocery Outlet failed the lock audit.
fleet.caveat: Needs the Web Unlocker on every run, so it is the only locked site with a per-run credit cost. Budget for it in the scheduler.
fleet.role_note: Scrapes cleanly and carries a distinct markup shape for the heal story, but its public catalogue does not contain plain staples, so it feeds scraper health and self-healing evidence rather than the price index. Interview decision: keep in fleet, exclude from index.

always_in_fleet.name: Parker's Pantry
always_in_fleet.why_locked: The clone store on the VPS subdomain. Disclosed test rig with a layout-mutation switch; it is the scripted break-detect-heal demo centerpiece per docs/prd.md section 2.5, not a real retailer, so it is not scored in the registry.

bench._comment: Named substitutes, already vetted, promote without re-running discovery.

changelog.why: A clean no-cache re-probe with TLS verification and a tightened price regex reclassified Grocery Outlet from server_rendered to spa_empty. Its original verdict rested on a homepage banner asset (012126_eggs_websitebanner_) that the product-URL scorer mistook for a product page; vet.py now rejects marketing-asset slugs. Meijer was the named bench substitute for the bare-HTML slot.

changelog.change: Split the fleet into index contributors and reliability subjects
changelog.why: Building the per-store basket showed the four US members settle 0-4 of the core 10 items - not a scraping failure but a catalogue one. Round 4 hunted specifically for US retailers publishing staples and found none across co-ops, Hispanic and Asian grocers, delivery-first grocers and US Filipino grocers. Sukli and Lili Mart both looked ideal on structure and both turned out to sell snacks and specialty goods. Rather than drop working scrapers or pretend they feed the index, each member now declares which job it does.

changelog.change: Added Ever Supermarket as an index contributor
changelog.why: Testing every store with a search API through its own search rather than its sitemap surfaced Ever at 10/10 core items - better than any locked member. The registry had it at backup because sitemap keyword coverage read 0/10, which is the wrong measure for a store whose catalogue is only reachable by query.

changelog.change: Added Shop Suki as an index contributor
changelog.why: Found by searching for PH grocers on queryable platforms after Ever showed that sitemap-derived coverage understates stores whose catalogue is query-only. The PH index now rests on six contributors rather than four.

changelog.change: Added Kesar Grocery and MexGrocer as US index contributors
changelog.why: The earlier conclusion that no US retailer publishes plain staples was drawn from the wrong segment. Rounds 1-4 tested supermarket chains, diet pantries and snack importers; US ethnic grocers were never tested through their own search or with bare-HTML extraction. Kesar Grocery sells generic staples and fresh produce with 11,987 products in its sitemap, and publishes no structured data at all - which is exactly why it stayed invisible. The US side now contributes to the index.
